title: Mitosis and Cell Division
text: Mitosis is the process by which a eukaryotic cell separates its chromosomes into two identical sets in two separate nuclei, enabling a single cell to divide into two genetically identical daughter cells. The process consists of four stages: prophase, metaphase, anaphase, and telophase, followed by cytokinesis (division of the cytoplasm). Mitosis is essential for growth, tissue repair, and asexual reproduction. In contrast, meiosis is a related process that produces haploid gametes (sperm and egg cells) with half the normal chromosome number. Errors in mitosis can lead to aneuploidy, in which cells have abnormal chromosome numbers, which is a common feature of cancer cells.
